pl-l4d26c4-d1e112.summary: Distinguishes three senses of indulgence: concession, remission, permission. In the New Testament there is permission of lesser goods and lesser evils: of lesser goods, marriage, which earns no palm but is a remedy; of lesser evils, that is venial, intercourse for incontinence. Marriage is conceded; such intercourse is permitted, that is tolerated, so that it is not forbidden.
claims: Marriage is a conceded lesser good.
Intercourse from incontinence is a tolerated venial sin.

pl-l4d26c4.summary: Distinguishes senses of indulgence: concession, remission, permission. In the New Testament there is permission of lesser goods and lesser evils: marriage, a lesser good meriting no palm but serving as remedy, is granted; intercourse for incontinence, a lesser, venial evil, is permitted, that is, tolerated and not forbidden.
claims: Indulgence means concession, remission, or permission.
Marriage is a lesser good conceded.
Intercourse from incontinence is a venial evil tolerated.
